newsitem.title: UK: BA in last-ditch battle for AA link - paper.
newsitem.headline: BA in last-ditch battle for AA link - paper.

text.p: British Airways Plc is involved in a last-ditch battle with competition authorities to prevent its proposed alliance with American Airlines being referred to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MCC), the Sunday Observer said.

"John Bridgeman, director general of the office of fair trading, and Bob Ayling, BA chief executive, are involved in face-to-face negotiations to try to agree a set of conditinos that will alllow the deal to be approved," the UK weekly said.
The Observer quoted industry sources as saying last week that if the two sides could resolve the current "brinkmanship," the deal could be approved within the next two weeks.

Britain's Department of Trade and Industry secretary Ian Lang has final say and is expected to announce that the two sides can go ahead without the intervention of the MCC, but only if they agree to the conditions now being thrashed out.
Lang was unavailable for comment on Sunday.

Bridgeman wants BA to surrender a number of runway take-off and landing slots at Heathrow to allow new competitors to get into the congested London airport, and prevent the BA-AA alliance dominating the Atlantic airways.
But BA is offering to make slots available only if conpetitors cannot acquire slots currently operated by their European partners, the paper said. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
